text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An angry mob in Kiambu near Nairobi lynches four suspected car-jackers and Nairobi police gun down an ex-paramilitary police officer described as a hard core criminal.
- The body of the late minister for research, technical training and technology, Zachary Onyonka, will be buried on November 2 in his Kisii home.
- Three directors of the Kenya Planters Cooperative Union call for the total liberalisation of the coffee industry.
- Sudan People's Liberation Movement says it is ready to discuss peace with the Khartoum government as long as talks are brokered by the Inter-Governmental Authority on Drought and Development.
- Anti-riot police seal off Murang'a town to ensure an investment company general meeting called by opposition FORD-Asili Chairman Kenneth Matiba does not take place.
- Ruling Kenya African National Union activist Amin Mohamed Alibhai, who contested a parliamentary by-election recently, is picked up by armed police officers outside Nairobi law courts.
- Seven people are killed and 10 are injured when a bus is involved in an accident with a trailer along the Nakuru-Nairobi road.
- State attorney urges the Court of Appeal to correct a misdirection in a criminal trial and substitute the death penalty for an armed robber jailed for 10 years.
- Supporters of rival candidates of the Kenya National Chamber of Commerce and Industry exchange blows during Kisumu branch elections.
